newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks soar as Washington reaches budget deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks soar as Washington reaches budget deal.

text.p: Wall Street stocks bounded higher on Friday, toppling several records in a sizzling run fuelled by news of an agreement between the White House and congressional Republican leaders to balance the U.S. budget.
The Dow rose 95 points to close unofficially at 7071. The rally brought the blue chip average's gains for the week to 332 points, eclipsing a record set just two weeks ago.
The rally was more than matched by an explosive showing in the broad market. Technology stocks surged, pacing the Nasdaq Composite to the largest one-day point gain in its history.

The session got off to a solid start with the release of monthly jobs and wage data. The report showed a smaller than expected rise in U.S. payrolls and a decline in the average hourly wage, alleviating concerns about wage-driven inflation.
Clouding the issue for analysts, however, was a stunning decline in the nation's unemployment rate to 4.9 percent, the lowest level in 23 years.
"The market dodged a bullet with the jobs number," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
"But the reality is, if you want to look at something that's going to cause a pre-emptive rate increase, it's unemployment below five percent," he added.

The data, which reinforced the impression of a U.S. economy growing at a solid clip without currently tripping the switch on inflation, prompted a sharp advance in economically sensitive sectors like technology and transportation.
The Dow Jones Transportation index jumped 61.65 points or 2.4 percent to an all-time high of 2605.83.
But investors held back from blue chips, checked by the surprise in the unemployment figures.
That concern seemed to evaporate when news of the balanced budget deal broke.
"For years, Fed Chairman (Alan) Greenspan himself has said a balanced budget would lead to lower rates," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"This market had been getting ready for a melt-up," he said, "and now here we are, knocking at the door of all-time highs."
Few issues were left behind in the market's broad advance. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by about four-to-one on heavy NYSE volume of about 500 million shares.
Significantly, small cap stocks once again outdid their large cap brethren. The Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks rose 2.4 percent, compared with the Dow's 1.4 percent gain.
"We had a huge rally, and for the second day in a row, the Russell outperformed the Dow," said Bill Meehan, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "I can't remember the last time that happened."

The Dow's closing level put it just about 14 points shy of its all-time closing high of 7085.16, set on March 11. In three weeks, the blue chip average has exploded with a 10.6 percent rise and nearly wiped out its month-long correction.
The whirlwind finish to the week had some arguing that, once again, a significant pause is in order.
"I think we've overdone it here," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

With respect to the balanced budget deal in particular, he said, "We're seeing initially a reaction that's very clearly positive but the benefits are all in the out years, so the real impact remains to be seen."
In individual issues, Novellus Systems Inc jumped 6-7/8 to 69-3/8.

Traders cited a variety of rumors for the advance, including talk of a merger or a settlement of the patent suit between Novellus and semiconductor equipment rival Applied Materials Inc. Novellus did not respond to inquiries about the rumors.
Applied Materials, which declined comment on the rumors, gained 3-1/8 to 57-5/8.
Fisher Scientific International Inc skidded 5-3/8 to 36-3/4. The scientific equipment supplier warned investors its near-term revenue growth would fall short of historic levels.
The S&P 500 index rose 14.44 points to 812.97.
The Nasdaq Composite rose a one-day record 34.83 points to 1305.33.
The Russell 2000 index rose 8.32 points to 353.98.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
